The season ran from 15 February to 22 November 2003. [[Atlético Sport Aviação|ASA]] were the defending champions. The league comprised 14 teams, the bottom three of which were relegated to the 2004 [[Gira Angola]]. [[Atlético Sport Aviação|ASA]] were crowned champions, winning a second title in a row, while [[S.L. Benfica (Luanda)|Benfica de Luanda]], [[C.D. Huíla|Desportivo da Huíla]] and [[Ritondo S.C. Malanje|Ritondo]], were relegated.{{cite web |url=http://www.portalangop.co.ao/angola/en_us/noticias/desporto/2004/9/44/Angola-Soccer-ASA-Win-Third-National-Title,951ffad4-b84b-4cc9-8259-5b19c153e034.html |title=Angola/Soccer: ASA Win Third National Title |publisher=ANGOP.com |date=27 Oct 2004 |access-date=17 Sep 2015 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304073802/http://www.portalangop.co.ao/angola/en_us/noticias/desporto/2004/9/44/Angola-Soccer-ASA-Win-Third-National-Title,951ffad4-b84b-4cc9-8259-5b19c153e034.html |url-status=dead }} Mateus André of [[G.D.
